page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor using the 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration provisions 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.6 GHz with a single thread per core, resulting in 4 dedicated vCPUs. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio.

The instance operates without local disk storage or hardware graphics accelerators, relying exclusively on network-attached storage volumes for persistence. Networking includes a complimentary public IPv4 address. Because each vCPU corresponds to an independent physical execution core without simultaneous multithreading, it eliminates hyper-thread resource contention for aarch64 workloads.

This server provides strong compute efficiency typical of modern Arm cloud hardware. The standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio is suited for containerized microservices, build pipelines, development environments, and moderate web application serving that do not require local NVMe drives or specialized vector acceleration extensions.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.2-16 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M Arm-based processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.6 GHz, delivering 4 single-threaded vCPUs without multithreading overhead. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM distribution. There is no integrated local storage or GPU accelerator bundled, requiring remote block storage for persistence. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By utilizing dedicated execution cores on an energy-efficient Arm architecture, the instance provides cost-effective compute capacity for a variety of tasks. Suitable deployments include cloud-native microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight application backends, and general web servers running on 64-bit Arm operating systems.
